papers.title: SPDAlign: Interpretable Riemannian Alignment for EEG Forward Modeling Shifts
papers.summary: Using a classic generative EEG model, this work theoretically shows that forward-model distribution shifts across sessions/subjects can be recovered via linear transformations on the Symmetric Positive Definite manifold, and proposes SPDAlign, which aligns domain means and corrects global rotations with Wasserstein Procrustes. Simulations and public EEG datasets show competitive domain-invariant EEG learning, while the globally linear framework provides interpretability for frequency ranges, spatial patterns, and cross-subject variability.

papers.title: Non-invasive Seizure Detection Using Wearable Wrist-worn Accelerometry and Deep Learning
papers.summary: In 79 patients undergoing video-EEG monitoring, this study developed a time-series ResNet deep neural network on single wrist-worn accelerometry data for non-invasive seizure detection, achieving 95.65% sensitivity, 0.15 false alarms per 24 hours, AUC-ROC 0.98, and AUC-PRC 0.67 over 5576 hours of recording. The results support wearable accelerometry for long-term ambulatory seizure monitoring.

papers.title: Beyond circadian: a yearlong prospective cohort study into human sleep using subcutaneously implanted electroencephalography
papers.summary: This yearlong prospective cohort study recorded subcutaneous EEG from 20 healthy adults and found that early summer had shorter total sleep time and lower REM sleep duration, while bright sunshine shortened sleep latency, greater cloud cover lengthened it, higher temperatures advanced sleep timing and reduced deep sleep, and weekends delayed sleep onset/offset/midpoint. Robust multi-day intrinsic cycles were not detected, and social jetlag of at least one hour occurred in a meaningful minority.

papers.title: Resolution-aware spectral parameterization reveals robust context-dependent aperiodic EEG dynamics during real-world table tennis
papers.summary: Analyzing the OpenNeuro Real World Table Tennis dataset from 25 participants with EEG, noise-layer, EMG, and motion recordings, this study used artifact-informed residualization and resolution-aware spectral parameterization to compare peri-hit spectral activity between human-opponent and ball-machine play. Residualized alpha and beta power was lower during ball-machine play, and the clearest context difference was a higher aperiodic exponent over posterior and parietal sensors during ball-machine play, with a focal parietal effect persisting across specifications.

papers.title: Lifespan Trajectories of Resting State Bipolar EEG Power
papers.summary: Derived normative lifespan trajectories of resting-state bipolar EEG power from 12,906 observations (ages 12–70) in 5,781 alcohol-use-disorder-free COGA participants across seven frequency bands and 24 channels. Found sharp power decreases from ages 12 to early 20s, followed by beta increases and mixed theta/alpha patterns, with sagittal and lateral trajectories similar within and between sexes but bipolar inter-frequency correlations showing striking sex differences.

papers.title: Detecting EEG index of arousal in sleeping patients with unresponsive wakefulness syndrome.
papers.summary: Nighttime polysomnography in patients with unresponsive wakefulness syndrome, minimally conscious state patients, and healthy controls showed that EEG spectral slope fluctuated with sleep stages and indexed arousal across all groups, whereas spectral entropy and Lempel-Ziv complexity indexed awareness and differed significantly between conscious and unconscious states. The findings support the two-component hypothesis of consciousness, separating arousal from awareness.

papers.title: The sleep EEG spectral profile of narcolepsy with comorbid obstructive sleep apnea more closely resembles narcolepsy than obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.summary: Retrospectively compared sleep EEG spectral power in 37 adults with narcolepsy and comorbid obstructive sleep apnea (NT-OSA), 77 with narcolepsy (NT), and 110 with OSA. NT-OSA showed spectral profiles more similar to NT than to OSA across polysomnography and MSLT, with several MSLT differences persisting after adjustment for apnea-hypopnea and arousal indices.

papers.title: Frontal lead in preterm functional brain maturation.
papers.summary: Analyzed 211 EEG recordings from 62 preterm neonates (25-40 weeks postmenstrual age) using convolutional neural networks to estimate functional brain age (FBA) and introduced a spatial difference metric (sd_FBA). Found a consistent frontal-occipital maturation gradient in functional brain activity, with frontal regions showing the highest relative maturity, contrasting with structural MRI findings.

papers.title: Distinct EEG microstate signatures across different pain types
papers.summary: Applied a harmonized EEG microstate analysis pipeline across three pain conditions—capsaicin-induced pain, non-chronic back pain, and chronic back pain—compared with matched controls or pain-free baseline. Found pain-type-specific microstate signatures: capsaicin pain increased microstate C expression and transitions toward C, non-chronic back pain showed lower microstate C occurrence, and chronic back pain showed lower microstate D global explained variance, arguing against a unitary microstate signature of pain.

papers.title: Decoupling Time and Space: A Temporally Conditioned Refinement for EEG Source Imaging
papers.summary: Proposes a two-stream framework that decouples global temporal representation learning via a Transformer-based Temporal Condition Encoder from per-time-point spatial refinement in EEG source imaging. Evaluations on synthetic data show improved spatial localization over classical and spatiotemporal baselines, especially in high-noise and multi-source regimes, and transfer to real EEG enables age-group decoding.

papers.title: Frontal aperiodic activity and sensorimotor theta clustering are differentially modulated by tDCS during proprioceptive training in Parkinson's disease: An EEG study.
papers.summary: Randomized 24 people with mild-to-moderate Parkinson's disease to active anodal tDCS over the supplementary motor area or sham, combined with proprioceptive training for six sessions, and examined EEG aperiodic activity, Lempel-Ziv complexity, and theta clustering during quiet standing. Found significant group-by-time interactions in frontal and central lobes, suggesting tDCS may accelerate a shift from effortful compensatory processing to automatic sensorimotor control.

papers.title: A Semi-Dry, Visually Comfortable c-VEP BCI with Short Calibration, Conservative Idle-State Behavior, and a VR Proof of Concept
papers.summary: Developed and evaluated a semi-dry, low-salience c-VEP brain-computer interface with slow flashing codes, asynchronous evidence accumulation, and conservative idle-state behavior in 30 participants. Achieved 99.8% accuracy with 33 s calibration and 4.3 s mean decoding in an 11-class keypad task, no spurious commands during a 2-min idle period, and 100% accuracy with 5.6 s decoding in a VR proof-of-concept, with high visual comfort but higher fatigue in VR.

papers.title: Involuntary facial muscle activity during imagined vocalisation contaminates EEG and enables emotion decoding.
papers.summary: Conducted two EEG experiments with overt (n=14) and imagined (n=21) emotional vocalization to test emotion decoding, achieving above-chance accuracy for both overt (78.1%) and imagined (36.4%) conditions. Surface EMG in five participants revealed involuntary facial muscle activity contributing to EEG patterns during imagined vocalization, particularly for happiness, raising concerns about EMG contamination in emotion decoding.

papers.title: Involuntary facial muscle activity during imagined vocalisation contaminates EEG and enables emotion decoding
papers.summary: This study investigated EEG-based emotion decoding during overt and imagined emotional vocalisation, finding single-trial decoding accuracies of 78.1% for overt and 36.4% for imagined vocalisation, with high-gamma and lateral channels being important. Concurrent facial sEMG revealed that involuntary muscle activity, especially a 'railroad cross-tie' pattern during imagined happy vocalisation, contaminates EEG and contributes to decoding, cautioning similar emotion decoding studies.

papers.title: EEG emotion recognition via multilevel entropy analysis: The power of entropy of entropy on phase dynamics.
papers.summary: This study introduced Entropy of Entropy (EoE) applied to EEG phase series for emotion recognition, comparing it with phase entropy, Shannon entropy, and amplitude EoE on the GAMEEMO dataset. EoE-phase features significantly outperformed traditional entropy measures, achieving 71.7% accuracy and 0.869 AUC with a Random Forest classifier.

papers.title: EEG Signatures Support a Shrinking Spotlight of Attention After Errors.
papers.summary: In a luminance-varying flanker task with EEG and hierarchical sequential sampling modeling, post-error adjustments involved frontal midline theta linked to increased decision threshold and faster drift rate, while posterior alpha/beta power scaled with drift rate and this relationship was enhanced after errors. The findings support separable roles of midfrontal control and sensory-specific attentional mechanisms in adaptive control.

papers.title: Evoked alpha oscillatory activity is suppressed by prolonged elbow pain and modulated by repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation.
papers.summary: In secondary analyses of two experiments using nerve growth factor-induced prolonged elbow pain, TMS-EEG showed reduced alpha event-related spectral perturbation and intertrial coherence at peak pain compared with baseline, and active 10-Hz rTMS increased alpha ERSP relative to sham without altering ITC. The results suggest evoked alpha activity as a candidate marker of pain state and neuromodulation response.

papers.title: Mental health risk stratification using heart rate variability and prefrontal electroencephalography: eXtreme gradient boosting-based classifier and latent class analysis-based subtyping.
papers.summary: Using simultaneous HRV and prefrontal EEG recordings from 147 healthy controls and 123 patients with major depressive or panic disorders, this study built a mixed graphical model to identify key features and applied XGBoost and latent profile analysis. The XGBoost classifier achieved 74.9% accuracy, and LPA revealed three patient subgroups: hyperarousal, relatively stable, and frontal EEG slowing, based on distinct HRV and EEG patterns.

papers.title: Beyond processed depth targets: frontal EEG patterns, brain vulnerability, and postoperative delirium in older adults.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
papers.summary: This narrative review examined whether frontal EEG signals beyond processed depth indices provide information about postoperative delirium risk in older adults, synthesizing evidence from randomized trials, systematic reviews, and observational studies. It concluded that processed EEG-guided titration alone does not reliably prevent delirium, but patterns such as reduced alpha power, burst suppression, and spectral slowing may reflect anesthetic sensitivity and reduced cerebral reserve, supporting contextual interpretation.

papers.title: Emotional Context Modulates Neural Prediction-Error Encoding.
papers.summary: This EEG study examined how emotional context modulates neural prediction-error (PE) encoding during reinforcement learning using a drifting three-armed bandit task with emotional images. Trialwise analyses showed that emotional context significantly moderated the relationship between PE and feedback-locked neural activity, with the strongest PE-EEG relationship in neutral contexts and attenuation in positive (early RewP) and negative (later posterior) contexts, while condition-averaged analyses showed minimal emotional effects.

papers.title: Strain-Decoupled Serpentine Heterostructured Hydrogel Electrodes for Motion-Artifact-Resistant Electrophysiology.
papers.summary: The authors developed a strain-decoupled serpentine heterostructured hydrogel electrode (SHGE) that suppresses motion artifacts by localizing deformation away from the sensing interface. The SHGE exhibited high fracture energy (23.4 kJ/m2), stable electrical output over 50,000 bending cycles, and strain-insensitive operation up to 70% deformation, enabling high-fidelity EMG/ECG with higher SNR than commercial electrodes and >90% accuracy in classifying eight human motions when integrated with machine learning.

papers.title: Reducing cognitive demand fails to mitigate choice overload: Multimodal neural and gaze evidence for effort conservation.
papers.summary: Two experiments manipulating cognitive demand (via high-attractiveness option sets or a shortlist tool) while recording eye-tracking and EEG found that reducing demand accelerated decisions but did not improve choice performance as set size increased. Multimodal evidence indicated effort conservation: narrower visual search, shorter fixation-related ERP latencies, and weaker occipital alpha suppression under low demand, leaving choice overload intact.

papers.title: An adaptive technical and behavioral approach for biomarker acquisition in autism with intellectual disability
papers.summary: The paper presents a participant-centered protocol combining adaptive EEG and eye-tracking with individualized behavioral supports to acquire biomarkers in autistic children with intellectual disability. Feasibility testing in 76 ASD+ID children yielded usable EEG data (>7 min) in 61% and sufficient eye-tracking data in 67%, demonstrating that inclusive biomarker acquisition is feasible in this underserved population.

papers.title: Desflurane Increases Hippocampal RAF-MAPK-MSK1 Protein Levels and Reduces CLOCK Expression: Sorafenib Attenuates Cognitive Impairment in Aged Mice.
papers.summary: In aged mice and HT22 hippocampal neurons, desflurane exposure increased RAF-MAPK-MSK1 protein levels and reduced CLOCK, accompanied by cellular senescence, synaptic imbalance, and cognitive deficits. The RAF inhibitor sorafenib restored CLOCK, attenuated senescence markers, and improved cognitive performance, suggesting RAF inhibition as a potential strategy for desflurane-induced cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Integrating longitudinal seizure, medication, and quality of life data into epilepsy eare: A randomized crossover study of an Epic-integrated dashboard.
papers.summary: A randomized crossover study evaluated an Epic-integrated Epilepsy Dashboard that consolidates longitudinal seizure, medication, and quality-of-life data versus standard practice in outpatient epilepsy clinics. Clinicians rated the dashboard higher for efficiency, completeness, and usability, and shared review of clinical information increased (73.3% vs 25.0%, p=0.02), while most patient-reported outcomes did not differ.

papers.title: Respiration and individual differences shape behavioral and inter-brain synchronization
papers.summary: This hyperscanning EEG study of 88 individuals in musical synchronization tasks found that instructed in-phase and anti-phase breathing increased inter-brain phase-locking and perceived social closeness but reduced behavioral synchrony. Inhalation was linked to stronger inter-brain synchronization but less precise behavioral coordination, and partners with faster spontaneous production rates led with alpha-band phase advances.

papers.title: Conditional Flow Matching for Single-Neuron Electrophysiology: Capturing Multimodal Responses Across Stimuli
papers.summary: The paper introduces a conditional flow matching generative model for single-neuron electrophysiology that captures multimodal voltage responses to identical stimuli. On biophysically detailed models of human cortical interneurons, the model reproduced feature distributions, spike-time structure, and excitability profiles, including coexistence of firing/non-firing modes near threshold and low/high-firing modes at depolarization block, outperforming a neural operator baseline.

papers.title: Diagnosing Lennox-Gastaut syndrome in adulthood: A scoping review of diagnostic challenges and age-related electroclinical evolution.
papers.summary: This scoping review of 45 sources (421 patients) examined diagnostic challenges of Lennox-Gastaut syndrome in adulthood and the applicability of 2022 ILAE criteria. It found attenuation or under-documentation of classical features with age, including fulfillment of ILAE seizure-type criteria decreasing from 73% in childhood to 41% in adulthood, and mandatory EEG hallmarks documented in less than half of adults.

papers.title: Dissociable EEG microstate signatures of cognitive and response inhibition deficits in obsessive-compulsive disorder patients.
papers.summary: A cross-sectional study of 91 OCD patients and 76 healthy controls used resting-state EEG microstates to investigate neural correlates of cognitive and response inhibition deficits. OCD patients showed increased microstate A duration/coverage and decreased microstate C duration/occurrence/coverage, with microstate C duration positively correlated with stop-signal reaction time and microstate C/D metrics negatively correlated with Stroop effect, suggesting dissociable microstate signatures.

papers.title: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation in drug-resistant epilepsy: A randomized, sham-controlled crossover trial with exploratory EEG and MRI response phenotyping.
papers.summary: In a randomized, sham-controlled crossover pilot trial of 14 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy, active transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation did not significantly outperform sham (mean seizure reduction ratio 46.26% vs 48.62%, difference -2.37%, p=0.604), but greater EEG beta-band attenuation in occipital and frontal regions was correlated with larger active-specific clinical benefit, and bilateral structural abnormalities/limbic involvement were more frequent among nonresponders.

papers.title: Quantitative assessment of cervical spinal cord injury: Methods, clinical utility, and future directions.
papers.journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesized 73 publications on quantitative assessment methods for cervical spinal cord injury, covering imaging, neurological scales, electrophysiology, biomechanics, wearable sensors, and AI. It concluded that current methods are insufficient alone and proposed a staged multimodal strategy integrating wearable sensing and AI to improve clinical management and prognosis.

papers.title: Quantitative EEG and EEG-Derived Markers of Severity, Prognosis, and Recovery After Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 33 studies (1,696 participants) evaluated quantitative EEG and related biomarkers after ischemic stroke, finding that greater EEG abnormality—especially increased slow-wave activity, higher delta/alpha or delta-theta/alpha-beta ratios, and higher brain symmetry indices—was consistently associated with greater neurological severity, larger lesion burden, and poorer functional outcomes, though evidence certainty was low to very low and no universal prognostic threshold was supported.

papers.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND REMOTE MONITORING OF CARDIAC DEVICES: A NARRATIVE REVIEW.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines the role of artificial intelligence in remote monitoring of cardiac implantable electronic devices, covering current AI tools for implantable loop recorders, investigational applications for predicting ventricular arrhythmias, heart failure events, and device failure, and future directions such as adaptive device programming and digital twins, while noting barriers in data quality, algorithm transparency, regulation, and privacy.

papers.title: Electroencephalography (EEG) and Quantitative EEG for Acute Stroke Triage and Post-Reperfusion Monitoring: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 15 studies evaluated EEG and quantitative EEG for acute ischemic stroke triage and post-reperfusion monitoring, finding promising but heterogeneous signals for acute stroke/TIA or large-vessel occlusion detection using slow-to-fast ratios, hemispheric asymmetry, and relative alpha/theta power, and for post-EVT/MT monitoring using QEEG slowing, frontal delta-alpha ratio, seizure detection, and neurovascular coupling, but no diagnostic domain was poolable and certainty was very low for diagnostic use.

papers.title: A case of acute lithium encephalopathy associated with elevated myelin basic protein levels in cerebrospinal fluid.
papers.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
papers.summary: A case report of a 50-year-old man with schizophrenia who developed acute lithium encephalopathy with coma after serum lithium reached 3.95 mEq/L, showing generalized rhythmic delta activity on EEG and elevated cerebrospinal fluid myelin basic protein (141 pg/mL) without pleocytosis or elevated IgG index, suggesting that toxic lithium exposure may induce central nervous system demyelination underlying prolonged neurological deficits.

papers.title: Axonal dysfunction precedes axonal degeneration in a mouse model of progressive parkinsonism
papers.summary: In the MitoPark mouse model of progressive parkinsonism, dopaminergic axons showed markedly reduced action potential-evoked calcium signals and impaired action potential propagation that emerged well before dopaminergic fiber loss and motor deficits. These findings identify early axon-specific physiological deficits that precede axonal degeneration.

papers.title: Safe electrophysiology-guided resection of an epileptogenic non-exophytic hamartoma at the floor of the fourth ventricle in a child.
papers.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
keywords: hamartoma of the fourth ventricle floor
papers.summary: A 15-year-old child with a non-exophytic epileptogenic hamartoma of the fourth ventricle floor underwent safe electrophysiology-guided resection, which produced promising results for seizure control. This case supports intraoperative neuromonitoring for resecting lesions in this challenging anatomical region.

papers.title: Optimizing neurogenic differentiation of dental stem cells: a critical review of induction strategies and functional validation.
papers.summary: This critical narrative review categorized neurogenic induction strategies for human dental stem cells from the past decade into growth factor-, small molecule-, and combination-based approaches. It concludes that most protocols lack electrophysiological validation and that generating fully mature functional neurons in vitro remains challenging.

papers.title: An inadequate over-parameterized Mössbauer spectral analysis for the mistaken detection of surface FeIV=O, in Nature Communications 16, 7642 (2025).
papers.summary: This letter argues that the Mössbauer spectral analysis in a previously published Nature Communications paper was inadequately over-parameterized, leading to a mistaken detection of surface FeIV=O.

papers.title: Implementation of beta-lactam Therapeutic Drug Monitoring in clinical practice: a prospective, comparative, interventional study in intensive care unit patients.
papers.summary: In a prospective, comparative, interventional ICU study, implementation of beta-lactam therapeutic drug monitoring did not significantly improve PK/PD target attainment on day 4 or day 7. Neurological adverse events were associated with drug overexposure and acute kidney dysfunction.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
